title: Restitution as a remedial interest
summary: The restitution interest concerns restoration of benefits conferred on another party, rather than the full value of expected performance or every loss incurred in reliance.
notes:
In the surgery example, the doctor’s fee benefits the doctor, while a hospital payment may be a reliance expense without being a benefit to that defendant. Algernon Blair later examines reasonable value of work and equipment supplied to a contractor. Restitution can be a remedy associated with a breached agreement or a separate claim based on unjust enrichment. Identify the benefit, its recipient, and the legal reason for restoring it.

The focus is on the benefit transferred, such as a payment, rather than every expenditure incurred in preparing to receive performance. The Mobil Oil note uses restitution after breach despite questions about whether the venture would have been profitable. A damages calculation should distinguish a transfer to the defendant from an expense paid to someone else. Restitution can also be an independent basis of liability for unjust enrichment, introduced at pp. 145–146.
